blogs.title: When “Angioedema” Isn’t: Dermatomyositis of the Neck
blogs.description: A rapid, practical approach to unexplained neck/facial swelling that doesn’t fit histaminergic or bradykinin-mediated angioedema. Highlights tempo (days–weeks), absent urticaria, normal C4/C1-INH, poor response to antihistamines/epinephrine, subtle myositis skin signs, and early CK testing. Includes a streamlined ED algorithm and airway considerations when dysphagia is lurking.

blogs.title: CK Is the New C4: Lab Clues in the Swollen Neck
blogs.description: Make creatine kinase a reflex test in ‘idiopathic angioedema’ with red flags. Walks through the lab constellation that points to myositis (CK surge, AST>ALT, elevated LDH) versus true angioedema (normal inflammatory markers, complement abnormalities). Pearls on when to send myositis panels and how bedside nailfold capillaroscopy can clinch suspicion.

blogs.title: SAE1-Positive Dermatomyositis: A Phenotype to Know
blogs.description: What anti-SAE1 dermatomyositis looks like at the bedside: prominent cutaneous disease, frequent dysphagia, ILD risk, and a measurable malignancy signal. Contrasts SAE1 with TIF1-γ and MDA5 phenotypes to guide counseling, screening intensity, and treatment selection. Practical takeaways from this case to anchor recognition.

blogs.title: The Dangerous Swallow: Recognizing and Managing Myositis Dysphagia
blogs.description: How to catch and manage myositis-related dysphagia before aspiration bites. Covers early SLP involvement, videofluoroscopic swallow, NG feeding, secretion management, and interpreting an extrathoracic restrictive PFT pattern. CT clues to aspiration pneumonitis and when to escalate airway support.

blogs.title: Imaging the Puffy Neck: Infection, Angioedema, or Inflamed Muscle?
blogs.description: Radiology pearls to separate Ludwig’s angina and angioedema from inflammatory myopathy. Reviews CT signs (strap muscle/retropharyngeal edema without abscess), MRI markers of active myositis, and how FDG-PET reveals diffuse muscle uptake while doubling as malignancy screen. Pitfalls that mislead clinicians and how to avoid them.

blogs.title: Hitting Dermatomyositis Early and Hard: Steroids, IVIG, and Beyond
blogs.description: A pragmatic regimen for severe dermatomyositis with airway/swallow involvement: pulse methylpred, early IVIG, and choosing a steroid-sparing agent when ILD is on the table. Where rituximab fits, timelines for response, serial CK and functional monitoring, and PJP prophylaxis options when TMP-SMX isn’t tolerated.

blogs.title: Don’t Miss the Nails: Bedside Cutaneous Clues in Systemic Myositis
blogs.description: Periungual telangiectasias/microhemorrhages, violaceous facial erythema involving nasolabial folds, and the Holster sign as low-tech, high-yield clues that redirect the workup away from ‘ENT problems.’ How to do quick nailfold capillaroscopy in the ED/clinic and common mimics to keep you honest.

blogs.title: Cancer Screening in Dermatomyositis: A Pragmatic IMACS Walkthrough
blogs.description: Translates the IMACS guidance to the bedside: use clinical features (DM, dysphagia), autoantibodies (SAE1), and demographics to stratify malignancy risk and choose tests. Builds a staged plan—CT/PET, labs, and targeted endoscopy—and outlines sensible surveillance intervals initiated during the index admission.
